items.prompt:
When water freezes, its volume
A) expands
B) shrinks
C) stays the same
D) disappears

Freezing water can break rock because the ice
A) pushes cracks wider
B) dissolves the rock
C) burns the rock
D) cools it only

Flowing water changes the surface by
A) eroding and carrying soil and sediment
B) staying still
C) making rock
D) adding sunlight
items.answer: A) eroding and carrying soil and sediment

steps: Flowing water erodes and carries material.

items.prompt:
Water can wear away rock chemically because it
A) can dissolve minerals
B) is cold
C) is clear
D) is heavy

What does flowing water do with carried sediment?
A) Deposits it elsewhere
B) destroys it
C) keeps it forever
D) turns it to gas

A good plan to test freezing water's effect on rock is to
A) put water in a porous material, freeze it, and observe cracking
B) only look at the rock
C) weigh the water
D) heat the rock
items.answer: A) put water in a porous material, freeze it, and observe cracking

steps: Freezing and observing cracking tests the effect.

items.prompt:
Water is powerful at shaping Earth's surface because it
A) dissolves rock, splits it when freezing, and erodes and carries sediment
B) does nothing to rock
C) only reflects light
D) is always frozen
items.answer: A) dissolves rock, splits it when freezing, and erodes and carries sediment

items.prompt:
Repeated freezing of water in a rock's cracks will
A) gradually break the rock apart
B) make the rock stronger
C) have no effect
D) turn the rock to metal
items.answer: A) gradually break the rock apart

steps: Repeated freezing breaks the rock apart.
